title: Divide-and-Remember: Recursive Action-Relevant Memory for Long-Horizon VLA Policies
abstract: arXiv:2610.00982v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models struggle on history-dependent manipulation tasks, where the current observation alone does not determine the action, and the policy needs a memory of the history. Existing memory methods decide what to remember by design, for example, keeping frames with large pixel changes, and show inconsistent gains across tasks. We view what to remember as an optimisation problem. From the POMDP formulation of imitation learning, we show that the optimal memory maximises the conditional mutual information $I(a_t; m_t \mid o_t)$ between the action and the memory given the current observation. Intuitively, this means preserving the action-relevant information in the history that is not already contained in the current observation. Based on our analysis, we propose Divide-and-Remember (D&R), a recursive memory method that learns a memory function $m_t = M(h_t)$ and scales to long contexts while staying compute-light

translated_title: 分而记之：面向长时程视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略的递归式动作相关记忆
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在依赖历史的操控任务上表现不佳，因为仅凭当前观测无法确定动作，策略需要对历史的记忆。现有的记忆方法通过人工设计来决定记住什么，例如保留像素变化较大的帧，并且在不同任务上收益不一致。我们将“记住什么”视为一个优化问题。从模仿学习的POMDP（部分可观测马尔可夫决策过程）表述出发，我们证明了最优记忆应最大化在给定当前观测条件下动作与记忆之间的条件互信息 I(a_t; m_t | o_t)。直观地说，这意味着保留历史中那些尚未包含在当前观测里的动作相关信息。基于这一分析，我们提出了 Divide-and-Remember（D&R），一种递归记忆方法，它学习记忆函数 m_t = M(h_t)，既能扩展到长上下文，又保持较低的计算开销。
tldr: 该论文将“该记住什么”形式化为最大化条件互信息 I(a_t; m_t|o_t) 的优化问题，并据此提出递归记忆方法 Divide-and-Remember（D&R），使VLA策略能以较低计算成本处理依赖历史的长时程操控任务。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes "what to remember" as maximizing the conditional mutual information I(a_t; m_t|o_t), and proposes Divide-and-Remember (D&R), a recursive, compute-light memory method that enables VLA policies to handle history-dependent long-horizon manipulation tasks.
